ἀπὸ μαστοῦ, θλίψιν ἐπὶ θλίψει προσ- δέχου, ἐλπίδα ἐπ' ἐλπίδι, ἔτι μικρὸν, ἔτι μικρὸν,
διὰ φαυλισμὸν χειλέων, διὰ γλώσσης ἑτέρας.9 Κατέληξε μὲν ἡμῖν ὁ πρῶτος λόγος
εἰς τὸ, Τίνι ἀνηγγείλαμεν κακά; καὶ τίνι ἀνηγγείλαμεν ἀγγε- λίαν; ∆ιερμηνεύοντες
δὲ τῶν προειρημένων τὴν δύ- ναμιν, λέγομεν ὅτι τὸ τῶν ἁγίων προφητῶν εἰσεκο-
μίσθη πρόσωπον ἐπιτιμώντων τρόπον τινὰ τοῖς ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραὴλ, ὡς εἰκῆ μὲν τοῖς
παρ' αὐτῶν ἐντε- τυχηκόσι λόγοις, ὠφεληθεῖσι δὲ παντελῶς οὐδὲν, καί- τοι καὶ
κακῶν αὐτοῖς, καὶ μέντοι καὶ ἀγγελίας προηγορευμένων. Καὶ κακὰ μὲν εἶναι τὰς
τοῖς εἰω- θόσι πλημμελεῖν ηὐτρεπισμένας κολάσεις διαβε- βαιούμεθα, ἀγγελίας τε
τὰς ἐπ' ἀγαθαῖς ἐλπίσι τι- μάς. Ὡς οὐδὲν οὖν τὸ σύμπαν ὠφελημένων τῶν ἐξ
αἵματος Ἰσραὴλ, εἰ καὶ ἀνηγγέλκασιν αὐτοῖς οἱ προ- φῆται τὰ παρὰ Θεοῦ, ἀπειλάς τέ
φημι καὶ τῶν ἐσο- μένων ἀγαθῶν ὑποσχέσεις, Τίνι, φησὶν, ἀνηγγείλα- μεν κακά; καὶ
τίνι ἀνηγγείλαμεν ἀγγελίαν; Σεσιγη- κότων δὲ ὥσπερ τῶν ἁγίων προφητῶν, καὶ
μέχρι δὴ τούτων τὸν οἰκεῖον στησάντων λόγον, αὐτὸς ὁ τῶν ὅλων Θεὸς τοῖς ἁγίοις

τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας τῶν διὰ Χριστοῦ θεσπι- σμάτων. Ἀνδρίζεσθε πρὸς
ὑπομονὴν, καὶ εἰ θλίψις ἐπέρχοιτο συχνή τε καὶ ἀλλεπάλληλος ἐγηγερμένων τῶν
πειρασμῶν, καὶ τῆς τῶν διωκόντων ὠμότητος ἐπιφυομένης ὑμῖν, καρτερήσατε

pass_a_gloss: Tome 2. [Lemma, Isaiah 28:9-11:] Those weaned from milk, those drawn away from breast, expect affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope, yet a little, yet a little, through contempt of lips, through another tongue. The first discourse ended for us at the 'To whom did we announce evils? And to whom did we announce a message?' And interpreting the force of the things said before, we say that the person of the holy prophets was brought in, rebuking in a certain manner those from the blood of Israel, as having come upon the words from them at random, and having been benefited wholly nothing, although both evils and indeed a message had been foretold to them. And we affirm that evils are the punishments prepared for those accustomed to offend, and message the honours upon good hopes. So, those from the blood of Israel having been benefited nothing at all, even if the prophets announced to them the things from God, threats I mean and promises of the good things to come, To whom, he says, did we announce evils? and to whom did we announce a message? And the holy prophets having as it were fallen silent, and having stopped their own discourse as far as these things, the God of all himself calls out to the saints, saying: Those weaned from milk, those drawn away from breast, expect affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope. For the undisciplined, he says, and very sick with unruliness, were thrust out fittingly, and having become without share of the salvation in Christ, they will walk toward destruction. But you henceforth, those called through faith toward knowledge of truth, those drawn away from the tutoring in the Law as from some breast and milk; those who of old received food befitting infants, and had a more untaught mind, but now have advanced to a mature man, to measure of stature of the fullness of Christ, and have moved over to the food fitting the mature, and have not remained inexperienced in word of righteousness: direct your own hearts toward receiving the new proclamation of the gospel way of life, of the decrees through Christ. Be manly toward endurance, and if affliction should come upon you, frequent and one after another, the trials having been raised, and the cruelty of the persecutors growing upon you, endure a short while, and for a short while expect the afflictions, so that you may also be rich in hope, I mean that beyond the human mind.
pass_b_english: “Those weaned from milk, those drawn away from the breast: expect affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope, yet a little while, yet a little while, because of the contempt of lips, through another tongue” (Isaiah 28:9–11).

Our first discourse ended for us with the words: “To whom have we announced evils? And to whom have we announced a message?” (Isaiah 28:9). In explaining the force of what was said before, we say that the person of the holy prophets was brought in, rebuking in a way those of the blood of Israel, because they had met the prophets’ words to no purpose and had gained no benefit at all, even though both evils and a message had been foretold to them. By “evils” we firmly hold that the punishments prepared for those used to sinning are meant, and by “message” the honors that rest on good hopes. So, since those of the blood of Israel had gained nothing whatever, even though the prophets had announced to them the things that come from God, I mean threats and promises of the good things to come, he says: “To whom have we announced evils? And to whom have we announced a message?”

But now that the holy prophets have, as it were, fallen silent and brought their own speech to a stop at this point, the God of all himself calls out to the saints, saying: “Those weaned from milk, those drawn away from the breast: expect affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope.” For the undisciplined, he says, who are badly sick with unruliness, have rightly been thrust out; they have no share in the salvation that is in Christ, and they will go on to destruction. But you, from now on, who through faith have been called to the knowledge of the truth; who have been drawn away from the tutoring of the Law as from a breast and from milk; who once received food fit for infants and had a less instructed mind, but have now advanced “to a mature man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ” (Ephesians 4:13), and have moved on to the food that suits the mature, and have not remained “unskilled in the word of righteousness” (Hebrews 5:13–14): direct your hearts to receive the new proclamation of the gospel way of life, of the decrees given through Christ. Take courage to endure. Even if affliction comes upon you, again and again, one blow after another, as trials rise up and the cruelty of your persecutors grows against you, hold out a little while, and for a little while expect afflictions, so that you may also be rich in hope, I mean the hope that is beyond human understanding.

choices.english: the person of the holy prophets was brought in
choices.why: The prophets speak Isaiah 28:9a; God himself speaks the lemma that follows.
Cyril glosses ἀγγελία as the honours promised on good hopes, set against the threatened evils.
ἐξήνιος of a horse that throws off the reins; paired with ἀνουθέτητοι.
ἀνδρίζομαι is to act like a man; the sense is courage in endurance.
